# LLM fixtures (`tests/fixtures/llm/`)

The mock adapter (`engine/llm/mock.js`) answers every model call from a file in this folder when
`MOCK_LLM=1`. It is selected **only** by that variable — never as a budget fallback (review M5.4):
when the month's budget is spent the router throws `BudgetExhaustedError` and the agent is skipped.
A missing fixture throws `MockFixtureError`; the mock never fabricates output.

## File name

`<agent>.<case>.json` — `agent` is a roster name (`ceo`, `hr`, `strategist`, `writer`, `qa`,
`analyst`; `analyst.*` landed in FEAT-203), `case` is chosen per call:

1. `MOCK_LLM_CASE_<AGENT>` (upper-case agent name, e.g. `MOCK_LLM_CASE_WRITER=bad`), else
2. `MOCK_LLM_CASE`, else
3. `ok`.

Page-keyed variant: when the call carries a page handle (the router passes `context.page`, or the
brand's handle) and `<agent>.<case>.<page>.json` exists, that file wins over `<agent>.<case>.json`
(e.g. `qa.ok.kaatdo.json`, `qa.ok.job_rez.json`; `qa.ok.json` serves RishtaPatra and any page
without its own file). QA claims cite brand-specific fact ids, so one `MOCK_LLM=1` run can answer
every page.

## Shape

```json
{
  "agent": "writer",
  "case": "ok",
  "output": { "...": "exactly what the model would return, validated with assertShape(OUTPUT_SPEC)" },
  "usage": { "inputTokens": 5800, "outputTokens": 900 }
}
```

- `output` (required, object) becomes the adapter's `json`; its `JSON.stringify` is the `text`.
- `usage` token counts are copied into the usage line; `costUsd` is always `0`, `provider` is `mock`,
  `model` is `mock`, `mock` is `true`.
- `agent`, `case` and the optional `page` are documentation for the reader; the file name is what
  selects the fixture.

Agent fixtures land with their agents: `qa.ok.json` (RishtaPatra claims), `qa.ok.kaatdo.json`,
`qa.ok.job_rez.json` and `qa.fail.json` (one claim without a fact id) in FEAT-104; `strategist.*`,
`writer.*`, `ceo.*`, `hr.ok.json` in FEAT-105 (every `*.ok.json` output must pass the agent's
`OUTPUT_SPEC`, review M7 prove-by in `tests/schema-dialects.test.js`). A `*.bad.json` fixture that
fails validation exercises the router's single repair call: the mock returns the same fixture again,
so the call ends in `AgentOutputError` after exactly two attempts.

## Per-agent notes (FEAT-105)

- **writer** — page-keyed by handle (`writer.ok.json` = @rishtapatra, `writer.ok.kaatdo.json`,
  `writer.ok.job_rez.json`), the same convention as QA, so one `MOCK_LLM=1` run answers every page
  with that brand's fact ids. Each output carries `artwork`, `slides` **and** `reel` (FEAT-201: a
  `kinetic` reel of 4 × 4 s, so a mock run never needs the network that a `capture` reel would): the
  Writer keeps the block the slot's format needs (image → `artwork`, carousel → `slides` + one `altText`
  per slide, reel → `reel`) and drops the others, so one fixture per page serves every cadence slot. The
  drafts they imply pass `runChecks` against the real brand files in all three formats
  (`tests/writer.test.js`). `writer.bad.json` has a caption of exactly 2,300 code points (generated, not typed).
- **strategist** — page-keyed too (`strategist.ok.json` = @rishtapatra, `.kaatdo`, `.job_rez`). Each
  includes one `reel` idea: since FEAT-201 (`features.reels` true) the engine accepts it and, because the
  model does not place it, auto-assigns it to the page's first open reel slot (the `applyOutput` test
  still covers the refusal with reels off). The `assignments` name the open cadence slots for
  `now = 2026-10-12T05:31:00+05:30` (Monday); for any other date they point at slots that are not open,
  the engine ignores them and fills the slots from the ideas by format instead (ideas are still appended
  with engine ids). `strategist.bad.json` lacks `assignments` (shape error).
- **ceo** — company-wide (no page). `ceo.ok.json` splits the budget 35 / 30 / 35; `ceo.bad.json`
  splits 50 / 40 / 30 = 120 %, which the engine's semantic check rejects (shape-valid).
- **hr** — see "HR (FEAT-204)" below; in Phase 1 `hr.ok.json` was a shape fixture only.

## Analyst (FEAT-203)

- **analyst** — company-wide (no page). `analyst.ok.json` is pinned to week `2026-W41` AND to
  `tests/fixtures/company-populated/state/metrics/2026-10.jsonl`: every number in it is a metrics value, an
  engine count/sum over those records, a window constant (48 h, 7 d, 28 days) or a calendar number of that
  week — the engine's `validateAnalystOutput` accepts it only against that company state, and the fixture report
  `state/reports/2026-W41.md` is byte-for-byte `renderReport(analyst.ok.output, engine)` (generated by a
  script from the metrics fixture, not typed; `tests/fixtures-integrity.test.js` re-derives both). Under
  `MOCK_LLM=1` the week rule is waived (as for the CEO) but the number rule never is: a mock Analyst run
  against any other company state — a dry run on a Sunday, say — fails after one repair and writes no
  report (`tests/analyst.test.js`). `analyst.bad.json` is shape-valid with `reach: 999` for @kaatdo in
  `perPage`, an observation and the Markdown, a number no metrics record holds → `AgentOutputError`
  "report number not in metrics".

## HR (FEAT-204)

- **hr** — company-wide (no page). `hr.ok.json` is pinned to month `2026-10` AND to
  `tests/fixtures/company-populated`: every `evidence` number is the stat `engine/agents/hr.js
  computeAgentStats` derives from that company's `usage/2026-10.jsonl`, `runs/2026-10.jsonl`, the drafts
  written in October with their `qa.json`, and `published.jsonl` (generated by a script, not typed;
  `tests/hr.test.js` re-derives every number with plain arithmetic). All eight agents are reviewed once; one
  change, writer temperature `"0.8"` → `"0.7"` (verdict `tune`). `tests/hr.test.js` runs it on 1 November 2026
  against a temp copy of the fixture → `hr/2026-10-review.md` + `hr/proposals/2026-10.json`. Under `MOCK_LLM=1`
  the month rule is waived (as for the CEO and the Analyst) but the evidence rule never is: a mock HR run against
  any other company state fails after one repair and writes nothing. `hr.bad.json` is shape-valid and leaves
  `qa` out of the review, quotes a Writer `qaRejectionRate` (0.6) the engine did not compute, and swaps qa's
  provider to one whose table lacks its model — `AgentOutputError` "evidence number not in stats" / "qa reviewed
  0 times". The fixture company's own `state/hr/2026-09-review.md` + `hr/proposals/2026-09.json` (written by the
  1 October run, September had no logs: every stat zero, one cautious Writer tune) come from the same
  `renderReview()` and are re-derived by `tests/fixtures-integrity.test.js`.
